Viloxazine, a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor, can increase the systemic exposure of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, including isavuconazonium sulfate, by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring and dose adjustments of the substrate are recommended as needed. 2. Vinblastine, vincristine, and vinorelbine can elevate the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised during co-administration. 3. Zafirlukast may increase the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Isavuconazonium sulfate can increase the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, including reducing zanubrutinib to 80 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 5. Zileuton and ziprasidone may elevate the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Acetazolamide may increase the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate through CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 7. Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of OCT2 substrates, such as amantadine, amiloride, cimetidine, cisapride, dopamine, famotidine, lamivudine, memantine, oxaliplatin, pindolol, pramipexole, procainamide, ranitidine, trimethoprim, and varenicline. The clinical significance of these interactions is uncertain, and caution is advised. 8. Anastrozole may increase the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 9. Cyclophosphamide may elevate the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is uncertain, and caution is advised. 10. Acetaminophen (oral, IV, or rectal) can increase the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Immunosuppressive agents such as abatacept, adalimumab, alefacept, ansuvimab, antithymocyte globulin (equine or rabbit), basiliximab, belatacept, bezlotoxumab, brentuximab vedotin, brodalumab, busulfan, and canakinumab, when co-administered with isavuconazonium sulfate, may collectively reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Alfentanil, alprazolam, amiodarone, amlodipine, azelastine, betamethasone (oral or topical), bicalutamide, bromocriptine, and bortezomib may increase the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Betrixaban levels may be increased by isavuconazonium sulfate through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. Monitor closely. 14. Drugs such as amobarbital, apalutamide, bosentan, butabarbital, and butalbital are contraindicated with isavuconazonium sulfate as they decrease its levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 15. Atazanavir is contraindicated with isavuconazonium sulfate as it significantly increases its levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 16. Capivasertib levels may be increased by isavuconazonium sulfate through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, including dose reduction of capivasertib when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 17. Bosutinib levels may be significantly increased by isavuconazonium sulfate through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Calcitriol may decrease the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Caplacizumab and isavuconazonium sulfate may collectively reduce immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely.
